open_points.subject: owner-session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine … and only to Registry's own origin” does not define the cookie's host/domain, path, SameSite policy, or whether a session created over local HTTP uses a Secure cookie; cookies cannot themselves be scoped to an origin's scheme and port.
open_points.question: What exact cookie attributes and local-HTTP behaviour enforce the stated browser boundary?
options: Use a host-only, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie and require HTTPS everywhere
Use a host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, adding Secure only on HTTPS
Define another exact host/path/SameSite/Secure policy
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only cookie with Path=/, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Secure, requiring HTTPS for every owner-interface sign-in.

open_points.subject: confirmation input binding
open_points.text: A confirmation is bound to inputs “kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order”, but neither the digest algorithm nor the canonical encoding, field order, treatment of absent values, Unicode, collections, or object characteristics is declared.
open_points.question: How are confirmation-bound values canonically encoded and digested so every implementation decides equality identically?
options: Declare a canonical structured encoding and a cryptographic digest
Store and compare a typed canonical value tuple instead of a digest
Defer a precisely named canonical encoding and digest to State 6
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-declared canonical binary encoding of typed values, including explicit absent markers and sorted keyed collections, hashed with SHA-256.

open_points.subject: request-id validation
open_points.text: A request id is “printable text of at most 128 characters, made from at least 16 random bytes” and “Registry checks its form only”, but printable text, encoding, minimum form, and which properties Registry can actually validate are not defined.
open_points.question: Exactly which request-id strings are accepted or refused?
options: Accept a canonical UUID syntax only
Accept a declared ASCII printable character set with explicit length bounds
Accept any nonblank Unicode text up to 128 code points
open_points.default_guess: Accept canonical UUID strings and refuse every other form.

open_points.subject: idempotency of other agent writes
open_points.text: R0-78 requires every agent-reachable write to have “its idempotency key as input fields when it writes … and its replay behaviour”, while A01 gives request ids only to add-room and publish; request-access, withdraw-pointer, register-session and end-session writes have no corresponding key rule, and some repeats change state again or are refused.
open_points.question: Which remaining Kernel writes carry idempotency keys, and what does each replay return after the first call has committed?
options: Give every Kernel write a request id and retained replay result
Declare stable target/session identity sufficient for selected transitions and give keys only to non-idempotent writes
Narrow R0-78 explicitly to add-room and publish
open_points.default_guess: Give request-access and withdraw-pointer request ids with retained replay results, while treating register/end by session identity as explicitly idempotent transitions.

open_points.subject: stage-1 authentication and authorization
open_points.text: A04 puts “the caller's authentication and its right to the operation” in one stage and says every failure within one stage is named, although a missing or unknown token identifies no service whose rights can be checked.
open_points.question: For an absent or invalid credential, is authorization skipped and only authentication refused, or must the answer also report an authorization failure?
options: Authentication is a prerequisite; invalid credentials produce only the common authentication refusal
Authentication and authorization are both reported even when no service is identified
Give authentication and authorization separate ordered stages
open_points.default_guess: Treat authentication as a prerequisite and return only the uniform authentication refusal when it fails.

open_points.subject: empty import selection
open_points.text: The owner may pick “any subset” of source projects, but A16 never says whether confirming a mapping with no picked project succeeds, writes a closure and audit entry, and permanently closes import, or is refused.
open_points.question: May an empty selection be confirmed as the one successful import?
options: Refuse confirmation unless at least one project is picked
Accept an empty import and close the operation
Accept it without creating the closure
open_points.default_guess: Refuse confirmation until at least one project is picked.

open_points.subject: scope of import malformation checks
open_points.text: Rule 3 says records only of unpicked projects “are neither checked … nor imported”, while rule 1 exposes “every malformed record” and rule 6 says “any malformed record refuses the whole import” without limiting that to picked projects.
open_points.question: Apart from the explicitly global upload checks, can a malformed record belonging only to an unpicked project block confirmation or appear in the mapping?
options: Ignore all non-global defects belonging solely to unpicked projects
Validate and show all records, and let any defect block the import
Show defects in unpicked projects but block only when their project is picked
open_points.default_guess: Apply global file-structure checks at upload, then validate and block only the records brought by picked projects.

open_points.subject: import file and closure digest
open_points.text: The mapping, confirmation, migration closure and audit entry name the import file “by its digest”, but the digest algorithm, whether it covers raw file bytes or parsed canonical data, and its representation are not declared.
open_points.question: What exact digest identifies an import file and binds the confirmed mapping to it?
options: Digest the raw uploaded bytes with a declared cryptographic algorithm
Digest a canonical serialization of the parsed import
Record both raw-file and canonical-content digests
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes and store its lowercase hexadecimal encoding.

open_points.subject: configuration item namespace
open_points.text: “The configuration holds exactly these items and no other” and “an unknown item fails the start” do not say which file, object, prefix or environment-variable namespace counts as Registry's configuration; a process environment normally contains unrelated items.
open_points.question: What exact configuration container or namespace is inspected for missing and unknown items?
options: A dedicated configuration file/object with an exact schema
Only environment variables under a Registry-specific prefix
A named allowlist while unrelated process-environment variables are ignored
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated Registry configuration object with an exact, closed schema and ignore unrelated process environment.

open_points.subject: configured secret representation
open_points.text: Each configured secret must be “at least 32 bytes long”, but configuration values have no declared encoding or decoding, so implementations can count characters, UTF-8 bytes, hexadecimal bytes or base64-decoded bytes differently.
open_points.question: How are owner credentials, service tokens and the backup key represented and converted to bytes for length, equality and constant-time comparison?
options: Canonical base64 encoding of raw secret bytes
Canonical hexadecimal encoding of raw secret bytes
UTF-8 text whose encoded byte length is checked
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical base64 for raw bytes, require at least 32 decoded bytes, and compare decoded byte strings.

open_points.subject: daily run after an import backup
open_points.text: The import backup runs even when the day already has a backup and “besides it, at most one backup is made per UTC day”, but missed-run logic starts only “if no backup was made that UTC day” and says kept backups alone determine whether a day has one.
open_points.question: Does an import-triggered backup count as that day's ordinary backup, especially when it occurs before 03:00 UTC?
options: It is additional and never suppresses the ordinary 03:00 backup
It satisfies the day's backup requirement and suppresses the ordinary run
It suppresses only a catch-up run, not a scheduled 03:00 run
open_points.default_guess: Treat the import backup as additional; still make the one ordinary daily backup at or after 03:00 UTC.

open_points.subject: backup encryption
open_points.text: A18 requires each backup to be encrypted with the backup key and unreadable without it, but declares no authenticated-encryption construction, nonce generation, key derivation, format version, or authentication-failure behaviour.
open_points.question: What precise cryptographic format makes a backup confidential and tamper-detecting across releases?
options: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption format using the configured key directly
Declare a versioned envelope format with key derivation and authenticated encryption
Leave the algorithm release-specific but require each release to declare and verify it
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope with a fresh random nonce, a standard AEAD algorithm, and authenticated metadata.

open_points.subject: temporary backup file prefix
open_points.text: A backup and check file use temporary names beginning with a release-declared prefix, and every start removes “every file left there under that prefix”; the text does not state that the final kept backup is renamed to a name outside that prefix.
open_points.question: Which exact names are temporary and cleanup-eligible, and how are kept backups distinguished so cleanup cannot delete them?
options: Temporary names use a reserved prefix and final kept names never use it
Cleanup examines an explicit temporary-file marker rather than a name prefix
Kept names share the prefix but are excluded by a fully declared filename grammar
open_points.default_guess: Reserve a temporary-only prefix and atomically rename successful backups to final names that cannot match it.

open_points.subject: backup status reconstruction
open_points.text: A missing, unreadable or stale status file is “rewritten at start from the kept backups”, while the interface must show “that last outcome”; kept backups prove successful runs but cannot reveal a later failed run or its failure outcome, and no behaviour is stated when no backup exists.
open_points.question: What outcome is shown after status information is lost or cannot be written, particularly after a later failure or when there are no backups?
options: Show an explicit unknown/reconstructed status
Treat the newest kept backup as the last successful outcome and discard knowledge of failures
Fail startup until a valid status file can be restored
open_points.default_guess: Show a distinct unknown/reconstructed outcome, plus the independently known newest kept backup instant if one exists.

open_points.subject: failure to write backup status
open_points.text: Every run must write its outcome to the status file after success or failure, but rule 6 defines retry and serving behaviour only for “a backup or a deletion that fails”, not for failure to create, replace or fsync the status file.
open_points.question: Does a status-file write failure make an otherwise checked backup count as failed, is that backup kept, and when is status writing retried?
options: Keep the checked backup but mark/report status as unknown and reconstruct at the next start or run
Delete the backup and fail the run atomically
Keep the backup and keep retrying status persistence before the run completes
open_points.default_guess: Keep the successfully checked backup, report status persistence as failed/unknown, and reconstruct or retry at the next start or run.

open_points.subject: empty audit sequence in backup metadata
open_points.text: Every backup records “the last audit sequence number it holds” and the check requires the audit log to end at that number, but a new store may be backed up before any audit entry exists.
open_points.question: What metadata value and integrity check represent a backup whose audit log has never had an entry?
options: Use sequence 0 as the explicit empty-log value
Use an explicit absent value
Omit the field for an empty log
open_points.default_guess: Use 0 as the last sequence of an empty history and require the first entry to be 1.

open_points.subject: audit-erasure replay after restore
open_points.text: R0-89 says recovery follows “the latest date audit entries were erased by”, and A18 says to erase before “the latest date the owner erased by”; A15 permits later erasure actions with an older cutoff, so the most recently recorded cutoff need not be the greatest cutoff already applied.
open_points.question: After restore, should the owner replay the chronologically last audit-erasure action or the greatest cutoff date ever applied?
options: Use the maximum cutoff date ever accepted
Use the cutoff from the most recent erasure action
Replay every recorded erasure action in order
open_points.default_guess: Use the maximum cutoff date ever accepted, which reproduces the cumulative deletion boundary.

open_points.subject: repeating an import after artifact-vocabulary removal
open_points.text: R0-89 says an import lost with a pre-import backup “may then be made again”, while A22 and A16 refuse an import file containing a pointer whose type the current release no longer declares; A18 permits restoring with a later release after store migration.
open_points.question: How can the permitted repeated import proceed if a later release has removed a pointer type present in the kept export?
options: Require replay under a release that still declares every imported type
Allow import-only recognition of types valid in the release that produced the export
State that such an import can no longer be repeated and narrow R0-89
open_points.default_guess: Restore and repeat the import under a compatible release that still declares all types in the export, then upgrade afterward.
